boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the command “Go, and buy yourself a linen belt” (web:Jer.13.1), fronted by כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הָל֞וֹךְ (oshb:Jer.13.1, byte tier) -- a koh-amar shape standing in a private commission to the prophet rather than a public oracle onset, that private-commission shape holding at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses). A second word-event opens the burial command, “Yahweh’s word came to me the second time” (web:Jer.13.3), spliced וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י שֵׁנִ֥ית לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.13.3, byte tier), and after “many days” a further time-and-place transition opens the recovery, “Arise, go to the Euphrates” (web:Jer.13.6), on וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.13.6, byte tier); the interpretation phase then opens its own word-event at 13:8, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.13.8, byte tier). None of these three internal onsets opens a fresh row: each keeps the same addressee, Jeremiah, and the same enacted sign, the belt, with no commission to a new audience -- the 13:6 transition moves the scene back to the river without introducing a second participant or hearer. Command (13:1-2), the burial-and-recovery performance (13:3-7, spanning the time-and-place shift at 13:6), and the interpretation (13:8-11, closing “the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah to cling to me”, web:Jer.13.11) stay one unit on that ground.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 13:3 and 13:8 as separate rows (one per word-event onset) was weighed and set aside: both introduce a phase of the same enacted sign rather than a change of addressee or scene, and a symbolic act's command, performance, and interpretation stay one unit unless a tier-1 seam of that kind intervenes.
literature_type_guess: enacted sign-act narrative: a worn-then-buried loincloth as a ruined emblem of covenant pride

boundary_rationale: A fresh commissioning clause opens the row: “Therefore you shall speak to them this word” (web:Jer.13.12), spliced וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.13.12, byte tier) -- a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation form rather than a morphological imperative, Yahweh commissioning Jeremiah to relay a new saying to a broad audience, distinct from the belt’s own interpretation just given. The identical opening run recurs inside the span at “Then tell them” (web:Jer.13.13), וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.13.13, byte tier; that pointed run, sweep: 4 verses), continuing the same commissioned speech to the same audience rather than opening a second unit. The commissioned proverb, “Every container should be filled with wine” (web:Jer.13.12), turns into a judgment against “the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem” (web:Jer.13.13). The neum-YHWH formula stands inside 13:14 at the accent break, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.14, byte tier), not at the verse’s end: two further negated clauses continue afterward to the verse’s own close, “I will not pity, spare, or have compassion, that I should not destroy them” (web:Jer.13.14). The unit’s actual close is corroborated by the fresh imperative address opening next at 13:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this proverb-oracle into the preceding sign-act row was considered: both concern the same belt-owning voice, but 13:12 opens its own commissioned-speech clause addressed to a wider audience rather than continuing the belt's interpretation, so the two stay separate.

boundary_rationale: “Say to the king and to the queen mother” (web:Jer.13.18) opens on אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), a discourse imperative naming a new addressee pair -- the king and the queen mother -- distinct from the plural audience of 13:15-17. The two verses form one short oracle: the royal pair's fallen crown (13:18) and Judah's captivity (13:19) belong to the same announcement, with no further seam between them.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 13:18-19 together with the material that follows through 13:27 as one royal-and-national poem was considered: 13:20 opens on a doubled ketiv/qere pair at its first two imperatives, feminine-singular שאי against masculine-plural שְׂא֤וּ and feminine-singular וראי against masculine-plural וּרְא֔וּ, with the intervening object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ carrying a masculine-plural suffix under either reading (all oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), while the feminine-singular forms לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ govern only the verse’s second half. The addressee does shift there under either reading, distinct enough from the king and the queen mother to keep the two apart, though the case for reading 13:18 through 13:27 as one sustained poem is not without force.

boundary_rationale: A new address opens at 13:20, though not immediately in the feminine singular: “Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north” (web:Jer.13.20) renders שאי שְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ וראי וּרְא֔וּ הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), a doubled-note verse whose two opening imperatives each carry a ketiv/qere pair -- feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere -- with the intervening object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ taking a masculine-plural suffix under either reading. The feminine-singular Jerusalem address itself begins only with לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ later in the same verse, and governs from there through the closing vocative at 13:27, distinct from the king-and-queen-mother pair addressed just before. The sustained indictment of Jerusalem-as-woman runs through the scattering sentence (13:24-25) and the uncovering of her skirts (13:26) to the closing apostrophe: “Woe to you, Jerusalem” (web:Jer.13.27), where א֥וֹי לָךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.13.27, byte tier) is the oy lexeme (sweep: 8 verses book-wide) -- a different word from the bare hoy, ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.13 and oshb:Jer.23.1, byte tier), that opens the woe oracles at 22:13 and 23:1; the vav-prefixed shape, וְה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.18, byte tier), stands here and, in its own pointing, again at 34:5 (sweep: 2 verses), both funeral cries, so this row is not typed woe_oracle. The span’s own divine formula is the neum-YHWH at 13:25, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.25, byte tier), not a koh-amar: the chapter’s four koh-amar sites, 13:1, 13:9, 13:12 and 13:13, all stand before this row opens.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Joining 13:20-27 to the preceding royal oracle (13:18-19) into one ten-verse row was considered: the shift from the royal pair's plural address to the feminine-singular Jerusalem address that governs from mid-13:20 is real, but the two share the same humiliation-and-exposure imagery, so the fold-together reading is not unreasonable.

boundary_rationale: “This is Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought” (web:Jer.14.1) renders the full header, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ עַל דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) -- the OAN/topical-header shape, attested at four sites book-wide (sweep: 4 verses: 14:1, 46:1, 47:1, 49:34). The header is kept with the drought description that follows (14:2-6: mourning gates, dry cisterns, cracked ground, the doe forsaking her fawn, the wild donkeys panting) rather than standing alone: no addressee or scene shift separates the title from what it introduces, and at the other three sites the same header shape carries its own attached content rather than standing bare -- 46:1 heads the whole nations collection, while 47:1 and 49:34 each head a single-nation oracle with its own attached setting. Framed here as judgment_oracle by its dominant content -- a report of covenant devastation already unfolding -- rather than superscription, since only one of the six verses is the bare title.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 14:1 as its own one-verse superscription row, separate from the drought description, was considered and set aside in favor of the larger bundled unit, since the description carries the row's substance and no addressee shift separates the header from what it introduces.

boundary_rationale: “Yahweh said to me” (web:Jer.14.11) opens וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּ֛ל (oshb:Jer.14.11, byte tier) -- a scene shift to private address to Jeremiah, instructing him not to intercede, distinct from 14:10’s pronouncement about the people at large. “Then I said” (web:Jer.14.13) is Jeremiah’s own protest within that same exchange, citing prophets who promise “assured peace”; “Then Yahweh said to me” (web:Jer.14.14) answers him on the same opening shape that carries the row’s own onset, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.14.14, byte tier; that shape, sweep: 13 verses book-wide), and the reply exposing the lying prophets runs through 14:14-16. The recurrence is not cut because it marks a turn within one sustained private exchange rather than a fresh commission -- the same shape carries the onset at 15:1, where a genuinely fresh reply begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row at 14:13 (Jeremiah's protest) or at 14:14 (Yahweh's extended reply) was considered: the addressee does alternate at each turn, the prophet addressing the deity at 14:13 and the deity answering him at 14:14, but both stay inside one sustained private exchange between the same two participants. That is unlike the seam four verses on, where the material closing at 14:22 is a communal plea addressed to the deity by a first-common-plural voice, a different speaker role and a different unit type, corroborated by the petuchah there (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only) -- so the dialogue here was kept whole while the seam at 14:22 into 15:1 was not.

boundary_rationale: “Woe is me, my mother” (web:Jer.15.10) opens אֽוֹי לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) -- another oy apostrophe (sweep: 8 verses book-wide, the same lexeme spliced at 13:27 above), here turned inward as Jeremiah's own outcry rather than a judgment against the city, a clean scene shift from the divine judgment speech just closed. device_notes: Jer.15.9, just before this row, carries a setumah. Within the span, setumah breaks recur at Jer.15.10, Jer.15.14, Jer.15.16, Jer.15.17, and Jer.15.18, closing with a petuchah at Jer.15.21 (single-witness, tier-3 WLC corroboration in the Prophets). Jer.15.11 and Jer.15.16, both inside the span, each carry one further note in the separate single-witness ketiv/qere inventory: the unpointed ketiv שרותך beside the pointed qere שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), and the unpointed ketiv דבריך beside the pointed qere דְבָֽרְךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.15.16, byte tier).
